articles.title: Google Launches Gemini Decisions API With Gemini Decision 1 at $0.10/M Tokens
articles.content: Google has launched the Gemini Decisions API , powered by a new model, Gemini Decision 1 ( gemini-decision-1 ). The Gemini Decisions API does not generate text. It scores up to 1,000 typed questions against one shared input and returns calibrated probabilities. For developers, this targets the small branching calls inside agents: routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading. Google prices it at $0.10 per 1M input tokens, with zero output tokens billed. TL;DR Size: Context is 262,144 tokens (256K) across shared input and all questions. Runs on: Google-hosted API only (Gemini Developer API, v1beta). No open weights or self-hosting. Performance: Leads 7 of 9 accuracy benchmarks in Google’s table, with the lowest calibration error. Best: 92.2% on JevBench (public split). Worst: 58.7% Macro-F1 on Amazon ESCI, its lowest score. It also trails Jev 1.14 on When2Call (79.9% vs 82.0%). Bottom line: Best: multimodal, calibrated decisions in 150-250 ms. Worst: not the cheapest; Jev 1.14 costs $0.68 vs $0.88 on the shared suite. What is the Gemini Decisions API? Gemini Decision 1 is a specialized multimodal model from Google built for closed-set decisions. It reads text, images, video, audio and PDFs in one prefill pass. Output token usage is always 0. Your code branches directly on the returned numbers. Each request has 3 parts: a model ID, a shared input , and a map of questions. The docs define 3 question types: noul (yes/no): returns the probability of yes, bounded between 0.01 and 0.99. choice : picks 1 of 2 to 255 options and returns normalized probabilities for every option. score : rates input on 2 to 255 ordered rubric levels and returns a probability-weighted score. Every answer carries a confidence value from 0 to 1. Google suggests routing low-confidence cases to a fallback or a human reviewer. Questions are scored in parallel and cannot see each other. How does Gemini Decision 1 work? Standard models decode an answer token by token, then your code parses it. Gemini Decision 1 instead scores your candidate options in one forward pass. Google reports median model compute of 50-100 ms and 150-250 ms end to end. That holds for inputs up to 16K tokens and stays nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions. Billing follows the same design. The shared input is billed once per request, however many questions you ask. Each question adds only its own instruction and criteria tokens. There are no thinking-token, transcription or OCR charges. Gemini Decision 1 benchmarks Google tested Gemini Decision 1 against 3 rivals. They are TypeSafe Jev 1.14 , GPT-6 Luna on OpenAI Decisions and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. All figures below are self-reported by Google. Refusals and safety blocks count as incorrect. Benchmark Gemini Decision 1 TypeSafe Jev 1.14 GPT-6 Luna (OpenAI Decisions) Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite JevBench (public split) 92.2% 90.0% 90.9% 86.6% Amazon ESCI (Macro-F1) 58.7% 56.7% 54.7% 47.2% New Yorker Caption (text-only) 79.7% 72.0% 68.4% 73.7% Mind2Web Multimodal 86.2% 86.8% 81.8% 78.0% PubMedQA 79.8% 78.2% 74.4% 77.6% Global-MMLU-Lite (non-English) 86.0% 85.0% 79.6% 78.8% When2Call 79.9% 82.0% 70.4% 60.9% MMAU (audio) 71.8% Not reported Not reported 67.7% Video-MME (no subtitles) 69.1% Not reported Not reported 63.3% Top-1 ECE (lower is better) 0.0250 0.0494 0.0721 0.2104 Total price, 7 shared evals $0.88 $0.68 $0.93 $4.14 Source: Google blog benchmark table . The calibration result is the clearest gap. Gemini Decision 1’s error of 0.0250 is about half of Jev 1.14’s 0.0494. That matters when you set confidence thresholds for automation. On cost, Google says it is nearly 5x cheaper than Flash-Lite across the shared suite ($0.88 vs $4.14). articles.title: Google Wallet adds digital home keys to open your front door smart lock with a tap
articles.content: TL;DR Google Wallet is gaining digital home keys, allowing Android users to unlock compatible smart locks with an NFC tap or hands-free using UWB. The feature supports select Aliro-compatible locks from Aqara, Schlage, and Nuki, with one digital key working across multiple locks in the same home. The functionality is rolling out to Google Home Public Preview users starting today, November 11, with wider availability expected over the coming weeks. Smart locks have already made getting into homes a lot more convenient than it traditionally used to be, and Google is now making that process even more seamless by bringing digital home keys directly into Google Wallet . Starting today, those in the Google Home app’s Public Preview will have the option to add their digital home keys to Google Wallet, allowing compatible smart lock owners to unlock doors by simply walking up to it or tapping their phones against the lock.
articles.author: Karandeep Singh Oberoi

articles.title: The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track
articles.content: From November 30th to December 4th, Amazon Web Services (AWS) will hold its annual premier learning event: re:Invent . At this event, attendees will become stronger and more proficient in various areas of AWS technology through a variety of experiences: keynotes given by AWS leaders, interactive working sessions led by AWS experts, and fun, immersive activities such as live entertainment and games at re:Play . There are over 2,000 learning sessions that focus on specific topics at various skill levels, and the AI/ML (AIM) track has more than 140 unique sessions for you to choose from. We’re here to help you identify the sessions that best fit your needs. Even if you can’t join in person, you can catch up with many of the sessions on demand and even watch the keynotes live. The basics: Session types If you can join us, then remember that we offer several types of sessions that can help maximize your learning in a variety of AWS topics. re:Invent attendees can choose to attend breakouts, chalk talks, builder sessions, workshops, and code talks. The breakout sessions are recorded and uploaded a few days after to the AWS Events YouTube channel , while the rest are live non-recorded interactive sessions. Here are the details for each session type: Breakout sessions: Attendees are in a lecture-style 60-minute informative session presented by AWS experts, customers, and partners. Chalk-talk sessions: Attendees interact with presenters, asking questions, and using a whiteboard in session. Builder sessions: Attendees participate in a one-hour session and build something. Workshop sessions: Attendees join a two-hour interactive session where you work in a small team to solve a real problem using AWS services. Code talk sessions: Attendees participate in engaging code-focused sessions where an expert leads a live coding session. Lightning talk sessions: Attendees watch a 20-minute demo dedicated to either a specific service or customer story (located in the Venetian Expo Hall or Wynn/Encore Upper Convention Promenade). With so many sessions to pick from, it helps to know how the pieces fit together. Here is how AWS thinks about its AI offerings, so you can decide where to begin and where to focus. The AWS AI stack overview and tie-in to re:Invent sessions AWS offers a comprehensive AI portfolio in the cloud. It covers everything from the physical infrastructure and AI chips that power AI workloads up through ready-to-use agentic solutions that teams can adopt today. Understanding how these services work together helps you navigate re:Invent and focus on the sessions most relevant to what you’re building. Figure 1: The AWS AI stack Global Infrastructure – It all starts with data centers designed and optimized for AI workloads. These facilities are built to handle the power, cooling, and networking demands that large AI training and inference jobs require. AI Chips – Running inside those data centers are two compute options: AWS Trainium , purpose-built for high-performance AI training and inference, and NVIDIA GPUs for teams that need GPU-based acceleration. Customers choose based on their workload, performance requirements, and cost targets. Data Foundation – AI is only as good as the data behind it. AWS Context connects your data across storage, databases, analytics, and search services, giving models and agents access to the right information at the right time. Models, Training, and Inferencing – This is where models get built, trained, fine-tuned, and served. Amazon Bedrock gives you managed access to hundreds of leading models from multiple providers through a unified API. Amazon SageMaker AI gives you full control to train, fine-tune, and deploy custom models on dedicated infrastructure. Many customers use both depending on the workload. Agent Development and Management – Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is where you build, deploy, and manage AI agents. It supports any model or provider mix, including models from both Amazon Bedrock and…

articles.title: Apple Invites App Updated With Two New Features
articles.content: The free Apple Invites app for the iPhone was updated today with two new features: hosts can now add polls to invitations so guests can vote on details such as a party's theme and food, and hosts can now add an "emoji effect" that floats across invitations. Released in February 2025, the Apple Invites app makes it easy to invite people to events, such as birthday parties and baby showers. The ability to create an event in the app requires subscribing to an iCloud+ plan with at least 50GB of storage for $0.99 per month, but anyone who receives an event link can RSVP for free on any device. articles.title: New York Forces T-Mobile to End Data Caps On Low-Income Plans
articles.content: New York has forced T-Mobile to remove a 50GB monthly data cap from its $15 low-income broadband plan after regulators found customers who exceeded the limit had their speeds cut by more than 97%, to just 650 Kbps. "Additionally, the [Office of the Attorney General (OAG)] found T-Mobile restricted [New York's Affordable Broadband Act (ABA)] plans to areas with 5G coverage, despite offering standard-rate 25 Mbps plans in 4G areas, and intentionally coded its website to hide affordable plans from search engines," reports RochestFirst. From the report: Under the terms of the settlement, T-Mobile must: - Eliminate data caps on its ABA plans and deliver guaranteed 25 Mbps download speeds. - Expand ABA plan availability to all geographic areas where it offers fixed-wireless home internet service. - Make its ABA webpage indexed and easily discoverable via standard web searches. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Prusa launches new carbon-fiber and carbon-nanotube-filled 3D printing filament for electronics manufacturing
articles.content: Prusa released its new Prusament PETG ESD on Tuesday: a carbon-fiber and carbon-nanotube (CNT)- filled, electrostatic-dissipative (ESD) PETG filament meant to protect static-sensitive electronics. While it’s great for enclosures for a Raspberry Pi, ESP32, and the like, Prusa is targeting the filament more toward electronics production than hobbyist use; however, it’s cheaper than the non-ESD Prusament PETG Carbon Fiber at only $56.99. Prusament PETG ESD Black 1kg - $56.99 Prusa isn’t the only one selling ESD filament; 3DXTech and Polymaker were first to the scene, but Prusa is the first to include carbon fiber alongside carbon nanotubes to provide the ESD properties, improving dimensional accuracy and minimizing warping. 3DXTech sells its ESD-PETG at $105; Polymaker’s Fiberon PETG-ESD is $65.98, but the Prusament PETG ESD is only $56.99 and is the only one with carbon fiber reinforcement. Non-ESD filaments are generally safe for electronics enclosures; many hobbyists use regular PLA, PETG, and ABS without any problems. And while the extra protection can be appreciated, Prusa positions this not for hobbyists, but for electronics production — PCB fixtures and holders for soldering, IC trays for handling and transport, holders for testing multiple boards at once, etc., as Prusa shows on the PETG ESD product page. It saves on manufacturing costs, reducing the need for CNC-machined ESD trays and fixtures, and can be quickly printed on-site with very little lead time. It’s not necessarily for big businesses only either, as indie hardware developers and smaller-scale manufacturers could use this filament to improve their production line without buying expensive ESD filament. Prusa has not yet published the datasheet containing details about the strength of the filament, but Prusa claims that the filament has increased stiffness and reduced toughness, similar to Prusament PETG Carbon Fiber’s properties. However, the amount of carbon fiber in PETG ESD may be different from PETG Carbon Fiber, as the latter’s purpose is more for strength than for electronics manufacturing. Prusa is known to use its own 3D printers to print its own components and use its own products for the 3D printers it sells, and on the product page, Prusa says it uses PETG ESD in its own production line to prevent overcoating the edges when powder coating its print sheets. While it isn’t the first or only ESD filament on the market, it’s certainly the cheapest, and when its strength profile is released or tested independently, it may potentially be more worth it than Prusa’s own PETG Carbon Fiber in certain cases.

articles.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture
articles.content: Every time a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server published in the AWS Agent Registry, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, gains a new tool or updates its schema, the registry record must be updated too. Without automated push-based sync, consumers discover stale metadata. For organizations managing multiple MCP servers across accounts, such a sync keeps catalog records current within an existing governance workflow. In most enterprise deployments, a catalog’s value depends on its freshness. If a developer deploys a new tool on Monday, but the registry record still reflects last week’s schema, consumers lose trust in the catalog. Stale metadata directly reduces registry reliability, leading teams to inadvertently build dependencies on inaccurate information. When an engineer adds a tool to an MCP server but forgets to update the catalog: Consumers miss out on the new capability entirely. Applications might call the tool using an outdated schema, causing unexpected runtime behavior or silent workflow deviations. Multiplied across teams, this lack of automation erodes trust in the registry. Organizations ultimately fall back on ad hoc discovery mechanisms like hardcoded endpoints, informal knowledge sharing, and stale documentation. In this post, we outline an event-driven architecture that automates these updates using AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge, and AWS Lambda. Architecture overview The following solution brings these services together into an event-driven pipeline that detects runtime changes and synchronizes them to the registry automatically. The architecture supports both multi-account and single-account environments: Single-account setup: For straightforward deployments, all components reside within Account A. Cross-account forwarding setup isn’t needed as events flow directly within Account A. Multi-account setup: This involves two accounts where runtime events from Account B are securely forwarded to Account A. Account A (registry account) owns the AWS Agent Registry, the Amazon EventBridge rule, the push-sync Lambda function, and CloudTrail logs. Account B (MCP server account) hosts the MCP server runtime and the Amazon Cognito OAuth provider used for authentication. The sample uses two accounts, but you can scale the architecture for multiple accounts, with Account A as the registry account and multiple AWS accounts similar to Account B for different MCP servers. The following diagram shows the end-to-end event flow for an update to an MCP server in Account B. The captured event is forwarded to Account A, where a Lambda function queries the MCP server for its tools and updates the matching registry record. Figure 1: End-to-end event flow for a cross-account MCP server update, from the CloudTrail event in Account B to the registry record update in Account A. The architecture uses five AWS services: AWS CloudTrail captures UpdateAgentRuntime API calls as management events. Amazon EventBridge routes matching events to the Lambda function, with cross-account forwarding supported. AWS Lambda queries the MCP server for its current tools, diffs against the registry, and updates the record if changed. AWS Agent Registry stores MCP server records and their tool schemas as the central source of truth. AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, brokers OAuth token exchanges securely, so the Lambda authenticates without storing secrets. How it works: business logic flow After it’s deployed, the pipeline runs the following end-to-end workflow: Trigger : A developer in Account B updates an MCP server, which calls the UpdateAgentRuntime API in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and AWS CloudTrail captures the event. Route : Amazon EventBridge catches the CloudTrail event and forwards it to the central event bus in Account A . articles.title: Google DeepMind Releases AlphaGenome 2 for Cell-Type-Specific Variant Effects
articles.content: Google DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2 , a DNA model that predicts variant effects in specific cell types. AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional sequence-to-function model. It reads 1 Mb of DNA plus a target cell state. Its predecessor averaged across bulk tissues. The new model resolves closely related cell types and adapts to unseen single-cell datasets without fine-tuning. It is available through the AlphaGenome API for non-commercial research. TL;DR Size: Input is a 1 Mb (1,048,576 bp) DNA window, human or mouse. Runs on: Hosted API only for now. Training used 2048 TPU v4 chips; weights come “upon final publication”. Performance: Beats fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1, Borzoi and Scooby on single-cell eQTL and enhancer-gene benchmarks. Best: 43% recall at 90% sign accuracy on TenK10K sc-eQTLs, versus 23% for AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned. Worst: Outside accessible chromatin, sign prediction AUROC reaches only 0.63. Bottom line: Best: cell-state conditioning from raw scRNA-seq. Worst: no local weights, non-commercial only. What is AlphaGenome 2? AlphaGenome 2 is a U-Net style model with a convolutional encoder, an 11-block transformer and a decoder. AlphaGenome 1 predicted a fixed catalog of thousands of tracks in parallel. AlphaGenome 2 instead predicts outputs for 1 condition per call. The condition is a 256-dimensional embedding. It modulates activations through FiLM layers in the encoder, transformer and decoder. Conditioning only the decoder or output layers gave minimal gains. Conditioning the encoder and transformer drove most of the improvement. Outputs cover RNA coverage, CAGE, splicing, chromatin accessibility, histone marks, TF binding and contact maps. CpG methylation is new. How was AlphaGenome 2 trained? Training runs in 4 stages: Pre-training across bulk data plus 3,977 single-cell RNA and ATAC pseudobulk tracks from 36 studies. Condition refinement , which tunes only the embeddings and FiLM layers. Distillation of 8 teacher models into 1 student, using mutated input sequences. Post-training that maps a single-cell expression encoder into the frozen model’s condition space. That encoder was trained on over 100 million human scRNA-seq profiles, largely from CELLxGENE. Researchers can pass raw counts and get a condition embedding. The docs allow up to 256 cells per call. How does AlphaGenome 2 perform on benchmarks? On GTEx tissues, median Pearson r for cross-tissue expression changes rose from 0.61 to 0.71. Within tissues, explained cell-type variance rose from 23% to 34% for scRNA-seq. The main result is on TenK10K single-cell eQTLs across 28 immune cell types. At 90% precision, AlphaGenome 2 recovered 30% of causal variants. AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned on single-cell data recovered 16%. Direction-of-effect recall rose from 23% to 43%. On held-out ENCODE-rE2G CRISPRi data, enhancer-gene AUPRC reached 0.78. AlphaGenome 1 scored 0.73, a Borzoi ensemble 0.61. The gap was widest for enhancers 100 to 2,500 kb away: 0.62 versus 0.48. For assay imputation, AlphaGenome 2 beat the Avocado baseline on 166 of 181 held-out tracks. On an unseen Parkinson’s cohort, it reached 41% recall versus 17% for cohort-tuned Scooby . How does it compare with other DNA sequence models? articles.title: Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 gives your old speakers and TVs a second life for $69
articles.content: TL;DR Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 brings older speakers, TVs, and other compatible electronics into the modern smart home. It supports lossless audio, local device control, Bluetooth connectivity, and Z-Wave adapters. The new accessory is available starting November 11 for $69 in the US and €59 in Europe. Not every device needs replacing just because it missed the smart home revolution. That old stereo gathering dust might still sound better than your shiny new wireless speaker , while your TV or heating system could be perfectly capable of following commands without an internet connection. Home Assistant wants to bridge that gap with a new accessory that gives yesterday’s technology a place in today’s connected home. The new Home Assistant Connect AUX-2 is a multi-purpose accessory from Nabu Casa, the company behind official Home Assistant hardware. Rather than adding yet another gadget to your home, Connect AUX-2 is designed to make better use of the ones you already own, bringing older audio systems, TVs, solar equipment, and more into an existing Home Assistant setup.

articles.title: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
articles.content: T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA). articles.title: Anduril says its first satellite can see adversaries maneuver in orbital night
articles.content: Anduril Industries has announced the successful demonstration of a new satellite-based sensor designed to track other spacecraft that may be hiding their maneuvers in Earth's shadow. Funded with Anduril's internal capital, the company's oven-sized satellite launched on a SpaceX rideshare mission in July with a package of tech demo payloads: an edge-compute processor, a power-management system adaptable to different mission types, and a long-wave infrared space sensor capable of detecting other objects in orbit. Anduril reported on the success of the tech demo mission Tuesday. The company's satellite, named Anduril-216, flies about 590 km (366 mi) above Earth, spending about one-third of each orbit in darkness. Anduril-216's night passes allow its infrared imager to shine. articles.title: Before You Add Another KPI, Ask These 10 Questions First
articles.content: KPI can give your business insights into their daily activity and performance. It gathers together key metrics such as productivity, operating costs, order fulfillment and customer satisfaction. It is important to think about which KPIs to include. Too many KPIs can cause confusion and if the metrics are not aligned to the objectives of the business then they can be pointless. Ask the correct questions to ensure that the right KPIs are included in your Operations Dashboard. Asking questions can help organizations understand which KPIs are relevant and gain insights into their business requirements 1. What is the main aim of the dashboard? The first thing to consider is what you want to achieve with your dashboard. Your dashboard should not just be a list of numbers, it should be providing useful information to staff and management. Think of what you want to achieve. Increase staff productivity? Reduce operating costs? Faster order fulfillment? Improve customer satisfaction? Identify any bottlenecks? It is important to know why you are measuring a KPI. You need to know what you want to achieve so you know how to measure it. Knowing what you want to achieve will help you choose the correct KPIs. 2. Which KPIs are most relevant for your operations? Depending on your industry, what you do and what your business priorities are will affect what KPIs to pick. You should pick KPIs that will give you the most useful insights into your daily activities. Common KPIs for your Operations Dashboard: a. Productivity & Efficiency : Throughput: Total units, orders, or tasks completed in a specific timeframe. Cycle Time / Lead Time: Average duration to complete a full process or deliver an order from start to finish. Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE): Combination of availability, performance, and quality (crucial for manufacturing or automated plants). b. Quality & Compliance First-Pass Yield (FPY): Percentage of products or services completed correctly on the first attempt without rework or scrap. Defect Rate / Error Rate: Frequency of errors, returns, or non-conformance issues. c. Delivery & Fulfillment On-Time Delivery (OTD): Percentage of orders delivered or completed by the promised date. Order Fulfillment Rate: Percentage of total customer orders successfully packed and shipped completely. d. Resource & Cost Utilization Inventory Turnover: How fast inventory moves or is replaced over a given period. Labor / Resource Utilization: Percentage of available staff or equipment capacity actively deployed. Cost per Unit: Total operational expenditure divided by the total number of units produced or processed. 3. Can the KPI be accurately measured? It is also important to know whether you can measure your KPI accurately. If your KPI cannot be measured with accurate data then it will not be useful. Question: Is the data available? Can it be calculated accurately? How often can you measure? Are the methods of measuring consistent across departments? Is the data reliable? For example, if you want to measure customer satisfaction you need to ensure you have a consistent method for gathering feedback. They should be easy to understand and measured using consistent methods. If they are hard to calculate or require too much effort then you may need to look for something easier. 4. Does the KPI have a clear target? If you aren’t setting objectives for your KPI then it can be hard to understand how well you are performing. Tracking a KPI without setting a target makes it difficult to understand whether performance is good or needs improvement. Establishing clear performance expectations for every indicator is important. For eg: These are examples and will depend on your business requirements. Ask yourself whether the objective is achievable. If you set an unrealistic objective then it could create unnecessary pressure. 5. Who will be responsible for monitoring the KPI? Ensure you have someone responsible for monitoring your key metrics. If you don’t…

articles.title: Ukraine Strikes Cause Permanent Data Loss at Russia's Yandex Cloud
articles.content: Russia's Yandex says 2.84% of customer data has been permanently lost following Ukrainian strikes on data centers in the country. "According to the company, recovery is impossible because of critical damage to equipment and the lack of backup copies on the platform," reports UNITED24 Media. From the report: Yandex clarified that customers who had previously enabled the platform's backup tools did not experience any data loss, as their information remained fully preserved. The incident has prompted the company to revise its approach to data protection and disaster recovery, particularly the default settings for cloud infrastructure. Under the updated policy, automatic backups will be enabled by default whenever customers create new virtual machines on Yandex Cloud. Users will retain the option to disable the feature manually through the management console. In addition to changing its backup policy, Yandex Cloud announced the launch of a new availability zone, designated ru-central1-f. The new availability zone operates from a separate location, improving the resilience and reliability of the services. The report says Ukrainian drones targeted three Yandex data centers in Russia over four days, beginning October 8 with a strike on a facility in the Ryazan region that houses two of the company's three supercomputers. A second attack hit Yandex's largest data center in the Kaluga region on October 9, followed by a third strike on October 11 targeting a facility in the Vladimir region that houses the company's remaining supercomputer. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.author: BeauHD

articles.title: Are Bitcoin Options Peerless Since Features Tend to Be Limited?
articles.content: Bitcoin options and futures became one of the most appreciated assets in the crypto market due to their diversification possibilities. Launching BTC futures in 2017 and options in 2020 by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) was a significant event for investors and traders, as they could leverage Bitcoin’s price dynamic without owning it. Each category has something unique. BTC options allow users the right to buy or sell the underlying asset, while futures work through an obligation to settle the contract. While this may seem like a disadvantage, professionals can make the most of these contracts by using control strategies like the stop-loss order to prevent the consequences of rising or falling prices, whereas choosing how to buy Bitcoin can help manage your portfolio better. Thus, the debate between options and futures continues, as each category benefits a certain audience. But are options better than futures? What makes Bitcoin options lucrative? Bitcoin options stand in the category of financial derivatives through which users have the right to buy or sell Bitcoin at a strike price (a specific amount), within a certain time frame before the contract expires. The first step in owning an option is buying a premium, which is the cost of opening a position. Working with options instead of straight-up Bitcoin allows users to settle a speculative position on whether the market will go up and down, so they don’t need an intermediary for the transaction. While this is a huge advantage, investors should still learn about how to read the room in options by the following terms: The Delta phrase signifies the sensitivity of the option’s price; The Gamma term measures the movements of the options; The Theta term shows how an option’s price decays over time; Trading Bitcoin options efficiently Users can trade BTC options for speculating on the coin’s price or to hedge against any risk on the market. That’s why speculative traders must adopt a different approach to capitalize on volatility. This could be buying and selling the same number of Bitcoins with the same strike price and expiration date to ensure a net profit. The method for hedging is known as a covered call, in which traders sell, or write a call option equivalent to the number of coins they already own. It offers the chance to offset some losses in the case of a market price decline, whereas a growth of the market requires selling the holdings. What about Bitcoin futures? Bitcoin futures offer the same chance to gain exposure to the underlying asset without holding it, just like options do. However, the difference lies in the obligation to buy or sell BTC. The contract between two traders states the terms for when it expires, including the amount of BTC to be traded for a particular dollar amount. These contracts can be: Standard: the traders agree to buy or sell the specific BTC amount at a certain price and date; Futures ETFs: the partial ownership in the investments is handled by managers; Perpetual futures: traders can see the target price for BTC without having to repay the other party at a specific time; Benefits of Bitcoin futures While they seem overwhelming to navigate, getting a hold of Bitcoin futures offers several advantages, such as the opportunity to open long or short positions. This makes profit achievable even in price declines through short contracts. Moreover, traders have easy access to leverage, so they can borrow funds to adjust their positions. But the disadvantages of BTC futures should make traders more cautions: There might be high fees involved compared to buying only Bitcoin; Futures are less intuitive to navigate, so beginners can be confused when operating them; The high leverage chances also increase liquidation risks, for which they need a maintenance margin; Who should trade Bitcoin futures and options? Those interested in diversifying their portfolio with futures and options should take small steps in approaching them. Generally, new…

articles.title: Google Says Gemini App Rolling Out on Apple CarPlay Starting Today
articles.content: Google has announced that a dedicated Gemini app on Apple CarPlay is rolling out around the world in several languages starting today, allowing you to have conversations with the AI assistant right from your vehicle's dashboard. Gemini conversations on your iPhone automatically sync to CarPlay, so you can continue a previous conversation or start a new one. For example, you can ask Gemini to "Give me my daily brief for today" and it can give you a personalized answer based on your information in apps such as Gmail and Google Calendar. Or if you are driving around and looking for a restaurant, you could ask "What's a quick lunch spot in downtown Austin that's easy to get in and out of?" To get started, make sure you have the latest version of the Gemini app on your iPhone. Then, tap on the Gemini icon on CarPlay to start a conversation. CarPlay gained support for voice-based conversational AI apps starting with iOS 26.4. AI apps that have already rolled out CarPlay support include OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, X's Grok, Microsoft's Copilot, Perplexity, and others. iOS 27 also added Siri AI support to CarPlay, complete with a Siri app. Gemini was already available within the Google Maps app on CarPlay. articles.title: Can No-Code Project Management Apps Ever Compete with Developer Creations?
articles.content: With an increasingly technology-reliant society, it is no wonder that more and more American businesses are turning to no-code tools like Pave to help create apps for themselves. Although traditionally custom-developed software offered a product that newer solutions struggled to match, it is estimated that in 2026, 70% of new enterprise apps will be built with low-code/no-code platforms. This shows a growing hope that anybody can use these platforms and get what their business needs. But many are still wondering how close no-code can get to the advantages associated with developer-built applications. Are they becoming more useful, or is it still wishful thinking? No-Code development No-code development provides a platform that allows users to build apps from prompts and configurable components; its aim is to lower the technological requirements for development, allowing more people to develop what they need at a lower cost and much quicker, but it has been said to lack the capabilities of a developer. Traditional developer-built apps are built by specialists with a focus on tailor-made apps with exact requirements to order and are usually associated with good results but can be quite costly to create and maintain, as well as have longer development times. But understanding whether or not they are comparable depends on numerous factors and, most importantly, on what your business needs. Customization: Can It Meet Requirements? No-code platforms can create workflow and automation apps around already existing business processes. This allows greater freedom than off-the-shelf tools and can meet a lot of the requirements for most businesses. Developer-built apps have a large amount of freedom to create highly specialized apps with highly technical functionalities, as well as heavily personalized interfaces and logic, which means that apps can be built for an exact function that cannot be provided elsewhere. For businesses that don’t need highly specific development but need a personalized app to assist their team, No-code platforms can meet their requirement, but can struggle with apps that need higher functionality. Development Speed: How Different Is It? When it comes to speed, no-code platforms have a distinct advantage . The platform itself provides much of the underlying functionality needed to make an app. This speed makes prototypes and iterations much faster to create and test. Developer-built apps take time in proportion to what is required. Development cycles and testing can also take more time depending on the team in charge of development. In addition, testing and debugging add time and require much more time. If your business can wait and the specialized nature is important, then developers can be worth the time investment. However, if fast implementation and use are more important, then no-code can be the answer. Adaptability: Can It Handle Changes? One of the key benefits of no-code development is that operational changes can be done almost immediately without conventional development. Working off previous creations, the fast-paced nature can match a workplace where workflows naturally evolve regularly. For traditional developers, big changes can be accommodated when needed, but modifications might require additional technical work. This can increase costs, as well as delay workflow, as changes take time to be implemented. A no-code platform is a practical choice for organizations that expect frequent changes that remain within configurable capabilities, due to the speed and ease of making changes. But apps might evolve into complex systems where a developer may still be needed. Accessibility: Who can do it? No-code app builders directly reduce the amount of specialist knowledge needed to not just create apps but to modify and maintain them. The ease of use also means that people who would use the app can help develop and customize the app to better suit them. For developer-built apps, the development is in the…

articles.title: Your TV Cable Is a 2.5 Gbps Network: How MoCA Saved My Three-Floor Home
articles.content: Give a MoCA to your home and turn your TV installation into a LAN! In this article, I will share my personal experience of getting in touch with and implementing MoCA ( Multimedia over Coax Alliance ), including why, how, which choices I made, and which mistakes to avoid. I hope that it can help anybody interested in starting on this path. 1. The Problem i.e. the Opportunity In 2024, I moved to an independent house built on three floors... plenty of room available and just an FTTC internet connection capped at more or less 70 Mbps. I did not have many exigencies in terms of devices and interconnectivity—just a couple of NAS units, a printer, a smart TV (at that time plugged directly into the router), some domestic appliances like smart bulbs, a pet feeder, and some video surveillance cameras. All these latter leaned on the 2.4 GHz SSID of my router. The most critical point was regarding my NAS units, which I decided to place on the upper floor along with the printer, and the best solution I found was just to set up a Wi-Fi mesh using an AP (TP-Link RE450). The Wi-Fi router was instead placed on the ground floor, thus the speed and the signal were quite poor, but with a slow FTTC, you almost don't notice it. Finally, after a couple of years, FTTH was delivered to my city and I quickly decided to upgrade my slow internet connection; I was lucky anyway since a 2.5 Gbps line was available, to which I switched immediately. And then... the situation became quite different. How can I take full advantage of this bandwidth and make it available in all my home? I suddenly discovered that at several points (especially on the upper floor) walls were obstructing the Wi-Fi signal so that I could not fully benefit from my router, which in turn is also capable of providing a Wi-Fi 7 signal; my internet provider released to my contract a ZTE ZXHN H6745 router which also features one 2.5 Gbps port and two Gbps ports, thus there is the room and the capability to distribute the signal in other ways than Wi-Fi. After a quick check, I discovered that the Wi-Fi signal on the upper floor and in one bedroom located on an intermediate floor was decreased by 50% up to 85%, jumping from up to 1 Gbps in Wi-Fi 7 close to the router to 400-500 Mbps on the upper floor, while in the room with the NAS units I could just get barely 100-150 Mbps and even less in the aforementioned bedroom. This could be acceptable for many applications, but not, for example, when backing up my laptop or moving large files to/from the NAS units, and moreover, who knows about any future usages? So, the first answer to this requirement must be obvious: set up a small LAN pulling cables up to your router, add Ethernet wall jacks whenever necessary, and a switch patched to your router which has, luckily, a port with proper speed. This was the first step and my first attempt. 2. Explore a hidden infrastructure First, I need to say that my home has several rooms, each of them equipped with phone and TV wall jacks. I counted in total 8 TV coax plugs (all working) and 7 RJ11 phone plugs (never tested and used, anyway they are there...) thus the first and less impactful option was to assess this spare infrastructure to enrich it with Cat.6 cables that could provide all the necessary speed and bandwidth. Fish-taping several times from all the wall jacks, I discovered that most of the plugs are connected to a daisy chain (see Picture 1), and this, of course, does not make things easier. I could not locate the ending point for all the plugs since, in 3 cases, the electrician used the same conduits for the AC cables and the phone, and I preferred not to touch them. Given that, I could assess that probably (but for sure not easily) I could turn into Ethernet 4 out of 7 phone plugs using "normal" Cat 6 cables, thus not specific CEI-UNEL 36762 C-4 according to Italian regulations. Anyway, to make a cable arrive at the router, I had to pull it through three different plugs and this, although…

articles.title: Google brings the standalone Gemini app and Gemini Live to Apple CarPlay
articles.content: TL;DR Google is rolling out a standalone Gemini app to Apple CarPlay globally, bringing Gemini Live to the platform. Unlike its existing Google Maps integration, the standalone app supports broader conversations and Workspace integration. The rollout begins today, November 11. Users need the latest Gemini app on their iPhone and must have used Gemini Live at least once. Google is expanding its AI presence on Apple CarPlay by bringing the standalone Gemini app to the platform starting today, Wednesday, November 11. For reference, CarPlay users have already been able to leverage Gemini’s smarts, albeit only in Maps . The development today takes things a step further. The new standalone app brings access to Gemini Live too, unlocking hands-free conversational assistance throughout your rides. The move has been a long time coming, especially considering that AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, and Copilot are already available on CarPlay.

articles.content: According to the Ramp AI Index, US corporate AI spending rose just 1.65 percent in October 2026. One percent of companies still drive 80 percent of revenue for OpenAI and Anthropic. articles.title: Bose recalls 670,000 Bluetooth speaker batteries due to fire risk — what to do now
articles.content: Bose has issued a recall of more than 670,000 lithium-ion battery packs used in the company's S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ Bluetooth speaker systems due to overheating issues. According to a Consumer Product Safety Commission announcement , Bose has received reports of the battery packs overheating to the point of melting, producing smoke or catching fire. Fortunately, no injuries have been reported. The recall specifically affects battery packs that include any one of the following six digits in the serial numbers: 083723, 078352, 084105, 078591, 078592, 084106, or 086409. You can find the 17-digit number on the label printed on the bottom of the pack. These packs were sold both with the S1 Pro and S1 Pro+ speakers as well as accessories, for between $100 and $160 from December 2017 through July 2026. The speaker systems cost $700. In total, 634,759 were sold in the US, with an additional 35,400 in Canada. What to do if you have an affected Bose battery (Image credit: CSPSC) If you have the S1 Pro or S1 Pro+ Portable Bluetooth Speaker Systems, Bose requests that you stop using the battery packs immediately and remove them from the speakers. You can still use the speakers connected to AC power. If you have an uninstalled battery pack, you just need to find the serial number and send it to Bose. Bose is asking owners to register and provide the serial number at http://www.bose.com/support/s1-battery-recall . The company is providing a free replacement battery pack. You'll need to dispose of the battery safely, which means do not just throw the battery pack in the trash or in used battery recycling boxes at retail or home improvement stores. Lithium-ion batteries must be disposed of differently from other batteries because of the greater risk of fire. You'll need to look up your local municipality's household hazardous waste collection center. You should contact the center because not everyone accepts lithium-ion batteries. They will generally be able to point you in the right direction. articles.title: Rand Fishkin’s Seattle game studio serves up first trailer for ‘The Snackbar at the End of the World’
articles.content: The chef in “The Snackbar at the End of the World.” (Snackbar Studio Image) If the eventual release of “The Snackbar at the End of the World” is a full-on meal for video game fans, news this week of the game’s first trailer should at least suffice as an appetizer. Seattle-based Snackbar Studio , co-founded by SparkToro founder Rand Fishkin and his wife, writer Geraldine DeRuiter , unveiled its debut title and Steam page on Tuesday. The hand-drawn narrative adventure RPG puts players in the role of a chef trying to save a struggling family restaurant in a magical version of 1960s Italy. The studio now plans to launch the game late next year, after originally targeting the second half of 2026. Snackbar raised $2.15 million from 38 angel investors two years ago, and the project began four years ago, according to Fishkin. The team includes five co-founders (Fishkin, DeRuiter, game designer Nicolas Kraj, lead programmer Miriam Cabrera and art director Francesco Mazza) plus about 10 contractors. In the studio’s description on Steam, players forage for ingredients in the “forbidden wilds” outside town, battling explosive tomatoes, chaotic zucchini and vendetta-driven poultry. They then cook dishes back at the restaurant before a tyrannical mayor known as the Sindaco can shut it down. The game mixes combat and stealth with cooking mini-games based on real-world recipes. The trailer is set to “’O surdato ’nnammurato,” a classic Neapolitan song performed by professional musicians recruited by the studio’s music director. Fishkin said he and DeRuiter both cried the first time they heard it. Fishkin is best known in Seattle tech circles as co-founder of SEO software company Moz and audience research startup SparkToro, and he more recently launched Alertmouse, a tool for tracking online mentions. DeRuiter, a writer and author, is Snackbar’s head writer. In a LinkedIn post this week, Fishkin recalled telling DeRuiter during the COVID lockdown that he wanted to fulfill a childhood dream of making a video game. Her reply: “Don’t wait. Do it now. I’ll do it with you.” In the same post, he said the game’s themes include found family and fighting fascism “even when there’s no hope you’ll win.” He called it a love letter to DeRuiter’s small family village in the mountains outside Naples, to that era of Italy, to video games, and to the many people both of their families have lost in recent years. Moments like hearing that song come often in the work, Fishkin said, such as when a new feature clicks or a new animation brings DeRuiter’s characters to life. He has always loved art without being good at any form of it. “I may not be able to create art, but I can enable it,” he said. “What a wonderful feeling.” There have been lows, too. The team spent its initial 18 months on the project with a contract agency that didn’t work out, losing money with nothing to show for it. Fishkin is glad they kept going, “even when it felt financially irresponsible.” The game is entirely human-made, and Snackbar’s no-AI stance is firm. “Geraldine hates AI with the fury of a thousand suns,” Fishkin said. He once suggested, just once, that she use Google’s AI Mode to find a synonym, and she was mad at him for the rest of a six-hour flight home from Philadelphia. Even if players, the rest of the team and the games media were fine with AI (and they’re not), DeRuiter alone would make it a no-go, he said. Still ahead are 10 to 12 months of finishing the game’s content, playtesting, bug fixing, marketing and launch prep. Fishkin called it daunting, but said team members have done it many times before, “even though it’s our first rodeo.” Fishkin is still juggling Snackbar with SparkToro and Alertmouse, and describes his role at the studio as mostly oversight and management. SparkToro is growing again, and Alertmouse recently hit a big milestone in annual renewals with high retention. He and his Alertmouse co-founders are putting more money into the company to…

articles.title: Anthropic built a model that beats Opus. It recommends Opus anyway.
articles.content: Anthropic just released a coding model that beats Opus 5.5 on two major benchmarks and can complete certain difficult tasks for half the cost. Yet in its Fable 5.2 announcement on Monday, the company recommended that most developers stick with Opus, calling it the “strongest daily driver” for coding and knowledge work. “Based on capabilities and pricing, Claude Opus 5.5 is still our recommended model for most everyday work, from coding to knowledge work,” Anthropic tells The New Stack. “Based on capabilities and pricing, Claude Opus 5.5 is still our recommended model for most everyday work, from coding to knowledge work.” Anthropic says Fable is intended for large software migrations, multi-agent builds and long-running research, but its performance data complicates the recommendation. The more expensive model can cost less to complete certain tasks, and the company’s proposed multi-model architecture adds considerations around delegation, context management, and execution costs. When pricier runs cheaper On FrontierCode 2.0, Fable 5.2 at High effort scored 45.3%, nearly matching Opus 5.5’s best result of 45.5%, while completing the benchmark tasks at roughly half the cost, according to Anthropic. Fable costs twice as much per token, at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens compared with Opus at $4 and $20, yet its reported task cost was lower, demonstrating that token pricing alone doesn’t determine which model is more economical. Anthropic also cited an internal experiment in which 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents formalized Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours. With the same agent configuration, Opus 5.5 completed only 26% after 18 hours and made little additional progress by the 30-hour mark, according to the company’s published results. The experiment demonstrates the scale of work Anthropic is targeting with Fable, although it doesn’t establish how much of that advantage carries over to smaller deployments or conventional coding workloads. Model manager mode The company is also positioning Fable as a coordinator for less expensive models, so developers can reserve reasoning capabilities for work that other models cannot reliably complete. “Fable 5.2 can act as an orchestrator that delegates simpler tasks to Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5, or as an advisor those models consult on harder problems.” “Developers also no longer have to choose just one model,” Anthropic tells The New Stack, “Fable 5.2 can act as an orchestrator that delegates simpler tasks to Opus 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5, or as an advisor those models consult on harder problems.” For a large software migration, Fable could analyze dependencies, plan changes across services, and delegate individual implementation tasks to Opus or Sonnet. More difficult decisions could then be escalated back to Fable without requiring the more expensive model to perform every step. Coinbase has already built a multi-model infrastructure that routes tasks based on requirements and cost, and the company says it cut internal AI spending by nearly half even as token usage increased. Anthropic wants Fable to handle some of those routing decisions itself, although any savings will depend on how often cheaper models can finish the work they’re assigned without needing help, since additional model calls, context transfers and failed attempts can drive up costs over the course of a long-running agent task. The context-switching tax There’s another complication when developers switch between models during a conversation. Fable 5.2 can read thinking blocks generated by Opus 5.5 , but Opus cannot read those generated by Fable. This could mean finding another way to pass along relevant context when building systems that move work between models, something that can require additional tokens, not to mention eat into the savings from using cheaper models. articles.title: Why Nvidia gave OpenShell to the CNCF
articles.content: Nvidia this week donated OpenShell , its open-source runtime for securing and governing AI agents, to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation. The teams that run it in production already work with Kubernetes and the CNCF’s other projects, says Ali Golshan, Nvidia’s senior director of AI software, who leads the project. The company announced the move on Tuesday at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City. OpenShell , which Nvidia launched at its GTC conference in March, joins the CNCF as a Sandbox project, the foundation’s entry-level tier for early-stage projects. The CNCF formally accepted the project in late September. The CNCF currently hosts 262 projects, including 155 at the Sandbox level, but it wasn’t the only possible home for OpenShell. The CNCF’s parent organization, the Linux Foundation, also runs the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF), which hosts agentgateway, the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol. Last month, the AAIF also took in OpenSandbox , a sandbox platform for AI agents that Alibaba contributed. “Securing and creating trust around AI is really infrastructure. That’s really where you need to start.” But as Golshan tells The New Stack , “Securing and creating trust around AI is really infrastructure. That’s really where you need to start.” That, he says, is what made the CNCF the logical place for the project to land. The platform team is the user OpenShell runs an agent inside a sandbox and enforces policies on which files, networks, credentials, and model endpoints that agent can reach. That enforcement happens in the infrastructure around the agent, according to the CNCF , and the project is adopting Cedar , another CNCF project, as its policy language. Golshan says that securing agents takes a full stack solution and that Nvidia couldn’t build that stack one piece at a time. “We can’t go build OpenShell and then go build the next pieces of it,” he says. “And a lot of those pieces, from an infrastructure standpoint, already existed in CNCF.” He cites Kubernetes itself, as well as the lightweight K3s distribution and service meshes, as examples of adjacent projects. While building OpenShell, it also became clearer who would operate it, Golshan says. The profile matched the DevSecOps engineer who already stands up the rest of a company’s infrastructure. He points to SAP as a company where DevOps and infrastructure teams stand up large agent environments. The people who work with the agents may be engineers or researchers, he says, but the operators are “the same teams that are spinning up Kube and Linux and that whole stack.” Ideally, those end users never see OpenShell. “You don’t really see Kubernetes,” Golshan says. “You just get that environment.” When Jonathan Bryce , the CNCF’s executive director, thinks about where a technology should live, he tells The New Stack , the question to ask is “where are the people who are going to be making the decision about deploying, using, contributing to a specific technology?” Agents started with people running OpenClaw on Mac Minis at home, Bryce says, but long-running, SaaS-style agents look more like other software run in a data center. Before OpenShell joined the CNCF, he adds, much of its early uptake came from neoclouds, GPU cloud providers that want to govern the workloads their customers run on their infrastructure. Since OpenShell plugs into Kubernetes and other ecosystem projects, Bryce says, teams that already run that stack can easily add it to the workloads they want to contain. Where agent projects live Agents will exist throughout the entire stack, Bryce says, and the open-source projects that support them will spread across several foundations, each with a different kind of contributor. articles.title: UltraVoxelGS: 3D Ultrasound From Tracked Sweeps in Seconds
articles.content: Hong Kong Baptist University turns tracked 2D ultrasound frames into a 3D Gaussian scene in about 10 seconds, no per-scan fitting. AI-assistance disclosure: I drafted this article with AI assistance, then edited it and fact-checked every number against the paper (arXiv:2611.11951). Freehand 2D ultrasound is still how most abdominal, vascular and musculoskeletal scans get done, and the sonographer builds the 3D picture in their head. Nobody sees which part of the organ was never swept until the patient has left. A group at Hong Kong Baptist University wants to change that with a live 3D view that keeps up with the probe. Yue Wang, Haoxin Chen and Xiaoqing Guo built UltraVoxelGS, a network that turns a sequence of tracked 2D ultrasound frames into a renderable 3D Gaussian scene in about 10 seconds, with no per-scan training. The paper is arXiv:2611.11951 and is accepted at NeurIPS 2026. UltraVoxelGS is feed-forward. Earlier neural ultrasound reconstructions such as UltraNeRF, ImplicitVol or Gaussian splatting fitted to one scan optimize a fresh model for every patient, which takes minutes. UltraVoxelGS predicts the whole scene in one pass of an already trained network. What UltraVoxelGS does The input is what a tracked ultrasound system already records: 2D B-mode frames, each with a probe pose from an optical tracker, an electromagnetic tracker or a robot arm. The output is a cloud of 3D Gaussians that you can slice at any probe position and angle, including ones the operator never held. Feed-forward Gaussian methods from photography do not transfer, and the paper explains why. They assume many overlapping photos of the same surface that look alike from different angles. Two ultrasound frames share at most a line, and the same tissue looks different depending on where the sound comes from, because echoes are direction-dependent and the signal fades with depth. So UltraVoxelGS works in two steps. First, it uses the poses to place every pixel of every frame in 3D and blends them into one fixed voxel grid (0.75 mm spacing in the paper). This is close to classic freehand compounding. Then a Transformer reads small 8 × 8 × 8 voxel patches and predicts Gaussians for them. It only predicts the thin slab of the grid around each frame, then averages Gaussians where slabs overlap. Because the network sees the grid and not the raw frames, the cost depends on the volume size rather than on the number of frames. Each Gaussian stores a direction-dependent echo strength and an attenuation value. The renderer multiplies the echo by how much signal survives along the beam path, so a structure under a strong reflector can appear darker, as it does on a real scanner. Nobody labels attenuation. It is learned only by matching rendered frames to recorded ones. The last piece is Render-time Appearance Adaptation. When you ask for a view, the method finds the recorded frame whose probe center is closest, briefly adjusts the appearance values (not the geometry) so the render matches that neighbour, renders, and throws the adjustment away. This step does most of the sharpening. Without it, the rendered slices look smoothed by the voxel grid. What they found The main real dataset is a public set of robot-held lumbar spine sweeps with probe tracking from 63 healthy volunteers, with over 3,000 frames per scan. The second is 100 simulated liver sweeps generated from abdominal CT volumes in 3D-IRCADb and CRLM-CT. The test is held-out frames: the method never sees them, and the render at that pose is compared with the recorded image. Building the scene takes 10.04 seconds per spine case, against 10 minutes for per-scan Gaussian splatting (3DGS) and 15 to 18 minutes for UltraGauss and UltraNeRF. On the spine data UltraVoxelGS also renders the held-out frames best, with a PSNR of 24.29 dB against 22.55 dB for 3DGS. On the simulated liver it is ahead on PSNR and SSIM but not on LPIPS, where UltraNeRF scores better. The same trained model handles about 300, 600…

articles.title: Court Says Trump Can't Use Leaks To Justify Spying On Journalists' LinkedIn DMs
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: The Trump administration's fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can't sweep in "a vast number of confidential sources" of random journalists "who have no conceivable relationship" to the Department of Justice's investigation, an appeals court ruled (PDF) Tuesday. The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted. The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. That left journalists unaware for far too long that their First Amendment rights had been compromised, judges ruled. "A request by the government to scoop up reporters' records wholesale and ascertain the identity of their sources would tip the balance against informed discourse in a manner inimical to democratic health," Wilkinson wrote. He criticized the lower court for approving the request simply because the records were technically feasible to collect, emphasizing that "serious security and speech claims are in tension in this case. There is space under law for both." While declining to quash the order entirely, Wilkinson also directed the lower court to reconsider a limited exception to the government's secrecy order that would allow LinkedIn to notify an attorney representing the news outlet under investigation. Bruce D. Brown, President of The Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press (RCFP), celebrated the ruling, saying: "This ruling is a big deal and will quickly become one of the leading opinions in the area -- one we will be quoting from it for a long time. The court recognized that confidential sources are the 'lifeblood' of investigative reporting and that dragnet demands from technology companies to reveal those sources violate the law." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: AWS gives developers a free local stand-in for its cloud, built from scratch by AI agents
articles.content: AWS Emulator began as a weekend experiment, when an engineer prompted the Kiro coding agent to build a passable version of Amazon SQS in 15 minutes. (GeekWire File Photo / Todd Bishop) AWS says its engineers didn’t write or review a single line of code in its newest developer tool, and the company is touting that as a selling point. AWS Emulator, released Wednesday, simulates AWS services on a developer’s own machine. It’s built from more than 400 API models covering more than 200 AWS services. Developers and AI coding agents can use it to test code without a network connection and without paying for the real cloud. The tool addresses a problem that coding agents such as Amazon’s Kiro and Anthropic’s Claude Code have made worse. Agents can write code faster than teams can test it against the real cloud. Agents check their work by running the code and reading the results, over and over, and doing that in the cloud adds delays and costs. The emulator lets them run that loop on a developer’s own machine. In an ironic or perhaps appropriate twist, AWS used AI agents to build the emulator. Agents also maintain it, testing it against real AWS and fixing the gaps they find. “The emulator was written entirely by autonomous agents. Our team hasn’t written or reviewed any of the code,” wrote Matt Goldberg, the AWS senior principal engineer behind the project, in a blog post . Goldberg compared his agents to himself as a kindergartner, too young to hold a crayon properly, who got yelled at by classmates for ruining a group drawing of dinosaurs. The problem wasn’t bad intent, he wrote, just a lack of competence. The answer, for agents, is clearly defined areas to fill in. “I think agents also need coloring books,” he wrote. The agents work from AWS’s public API models, which describe how each service should behave, and check their work against the real AWS cloud. The agents run on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore in three teams. One writes “fidelity tests” — real-world scenarios such as creating a queue, sending a message and deleting the queue — and checks each against real AWS. A second runs those tests against the emulator and files issues for failures, and a third fixes them, one agent per issue. Every change passes through an automated gate where other agents check coding standards and security. Goldberg wrote that hundreds of agents now fix thousands of issues a day. The project started as a weekend experiment, inspired by Anthropic’s demonstration earlier this year in which a team of Claude agents built a C compiler . Goldberg gave Kiro a three-step prompt and got a passable first version of Amazon SQS, AWS’s message queuing service, in 15 minutes. By the end of the weekend, Goldberg wrote, Kiro had built a rough version of the rest of AWS, with obvious gaps, and his team started using it to test its software that Monday. Swami Sivasubramanian, AWS vice president of agentic AI and emerging tech, tied the project to a lesson he described to GeekWire in June. He spent four nights babysitting Kiro as it tried to rebuild a replication engine he and Allan Vermeulen built by hand nearly 20 years ago. Once he gave the agent a spec and a way to test its work, the job took about two hours. “When agents write the code and check their own work, the engineer’s job is to give them room to work on their own and to build the specs, tests, and merge gates that decide when that work is correct,” Sivasubramanian wrote in a guest post on CTO Werner Vogels’ blog. It’s the same idea behind Amazon’s recent move to rewrite its engineering playbook for an era when AI writes the code. The emulator has limits. Devin Pratt, an IDC analyst, told InfoWorld that it doesn’t yet simulate throttling, outages or differences in which services and features are available by region, and that it doesn’t sandbox the code it runs. The agents’…

articles.title: Tech Moves: Wizards of the Coasts names president; new execs at Skydance, Pulumi, Marchex and Syndio
articles.content: Dan Ayoub. (LinkedIn Photo) — Dan Ayoub , the past head of Dungeons & Dragons, has been named president of Wizards of the Coast & Hasbro Digital Games . Ayoub joined the Renton, Wash.-based Wizards of the Coast in 2022 and counts himself among the longtime players of D&D and Magic: The Gathering. “D&D is 52 years old. Magic is 33. Brands don’t last that long because of any one leader; they last because generations of creators and fans keep choosing them,” Ayoub said . “We owe it to them to protect what makes these worlds special.” Earlier in his career, Ayoub spent more than a decade at Microsoft, primarily with its 343 Industries video game studio, now called Halo Studios. Farah Ali. (LinkedIn Photo) — Farah Ali has joined the media company Skydance as vice president of engineering, based at its Bellevue, Wash., office. She previously spent a decade at Electronic Arts over two stints, most recently as vice president of AI transformation and technology. Ali has also served as an affiliate professor at the University of Washington, teaching courses in software entrepreneurship, and as a technical advisor for Madrona Venture Labs. She was co-founder and chief technology officer of FreightWeb, a Seattle-based logistics technology startup. Paramount Skydance last month completed its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), with the combined company taking the name Skydance. Shortly after, the company announced the departure of two WBD leaders from the Bellevue site: Avi Saxena and Tyler Whitworth . Irene Chang. (LinkedIn Photo) — Irene Chang has joined Pulumi as chief revenue officer. The Seattle startup automates cloud infrastructure tasks such as managing networks and databases, optimizing costs and ensuring compliance. Chang said Pulumi’s culture and product won her over. “We automate deployments so teams can provision resources in seconds and scale from simple apps to enterprise architectures without losing control or compliance,” she wrote on LinkedIn. Chang was previously Postman’s VP of corporate sales for the Americas and before that held VP roles at Cloudflare. Pulumi is No. 15 on the GeekWire 200 , a ranked index of the Pacific Northwest’s top startups. Travis Fairchild. (LinkedIn Photo) — Marchex , the Seattle-based, publicly traded call and conversation analytics company, has named Travis Fairchild as president. The news was disclosed in an SEC filing . Fairchild was previously with Marchex for 18 years in strategy and business development roles. He left in 2021 to become CEO of Archenia, a Las Vegas-based customer qualification and acquisition company, which Marchex acquired in July. Troy Hartless , who in September 2025 added president to his role as chief revenue officer, will return to serving solely as CRO. David Janashvili. (LinkedIn Photo) — General Fusion has named David Janashvili as chief financial officer, effective Nov. 30. The Vancouver, B.C.-based company is developing fusion energy devices and became the first fusion venture to go public , through a SPAC. It trades on Nasdaq as GFUZ. Janashvili joins from Surami Partners, which provides financial services for clean tech companies, and previously led climate tech investment banking at CIBC Capital Markets. Across numerous roles, he has advised boards and management teams of public and soon-to-be public companies. Tammi Kroll. (LinkedIn Photo) — Gravity Payments has appointed CEO Tammi Kroll as chairman of its board of directors while she continues to lead the digital payments company. “Her appointment as Chairman recognizes more than a decade of leadership at Gravity and her role in helping the company grow while remaining focused on the independent businesses and employees it serves,” the company said. Kroll joined the company in 2015 as CTO, chief operating officer and chief information officer. She took over as CEO in 2022 after founder Dan Price resigned while facing…

articles.title: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code verified Signal's cryptographic core in four weeks instead of years
articles.content: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Code mathematically verified Signal's cryptographic core code in four weeks, a process that typically takes years. AI agents powered by Gemini Carbon wrote more than six million lines of proof code and flagged only about one percent for human review. Deepmind plans to extend the method to critical infrastructure like power grids and medical devices. articles.title: Taiwan’s chipmaking giant TSMC to invest $1B in Anthropic, OpenAI
articles.content: Top chip manufacturer TSMC is ready to invest $1 billion in Anthropic and OpenAI. That would give the Taiwanese chipmaker direct stakes in leading AI developers, even as its own contract chipmaking business has profited enormously from the AI data center buildout. The chipmaker’s board approved plans to invest up to $500 million in OpenAI preferred stock reserved for large investors and another $500 million to purchase Anthropic common shares at the latter’s expected IPO price, according to Reuters . Such an investment may give markets “a shot of confidence as the artificial-intelligence trade shows signs of strain,” The Wall Street Journal reported. But analysts also warned that such circular financing among investors, suppliers, and customers has made it difficult to evaluate real market demand for AI-related hardware and services, according to the Journal. articles.title: Anthropic targets workplace collaboration with Claude Meetings
articles.content: Anthropic has expanded the range of productivity and collaboration features in Claude with the launch of spreadsheet, whiteboard, and meeting assistant tools aimed at knowledge workers. The features add to the Claude Docs and Slides features announced in September, as Anthropic equips its AI assistant for a wider range of productivity tasks. “Anthropic is moving Claude from a place you go to ask a question to a place where teams do their work,” said Craig Durr , chief analyst at The Collab Collective. One of the new tools announced Tuesday is Claude Meetings. This lets users add Claude to video meetings, where it takes notes, answers questions in the call’s chat interface, retrieves information from connected apps, and creates project plans and timelines. After a call, notes and action items are available in claude.ai, the browser-based version of Claude. Claude Meetings is reportedly accessible only in Google Meet currently; Anthropic hasn’t responded to a request for further details The launch of Claude Meetings highlights the “continued value of leveraging context within meetings to improve workflows,” said Irwin Lazar , principal analyst at Metrigy. Claude Meetings has similar functionality to existing meeting assistants, such as Copilot in Microsoft Teams, Zoom My Notes, and Webex’s meeting agent, he said, and also competes with standalone meeting assistants, such as Otter and Granola. “As Claude increasingly becomes the place where people are doing their work, it makes sense for Claude to have direct access to meeting notes without requiring cut/paste, or MCP access, which vendors like Zoom now charge for,” said Lazar. But while Anthropic is increasingly seeking to compete with office productivity suites, he doesn’t expect the company will venture further into developing collaboration and communication software any time soon. Email, calling, and video meeting software “all require far more extensive capabilities and infrastructure,” he noted. For IT teams that enable Claude Meetings, Durr recommends establishing procedures for obtaining meeting participants’ consent to its presence, in accordance with local laws. It already requires admin approval to attend calls including external guests; if approval is not granted, it will leave the meeting. “Claude identifies itself and posts a notice in the meeting chat, but recording and consent rules vary by jurisdiction and by company policy,” he said. “IT, legal, and HR should agree on when Claude is allowed into a meeting before it’s rolled out.” IT teams should also monitor the availability of new functions that might change the way Claude Meetings functions, Durr advised. The tool currently only acts when instructed by users, but could become “more proactive” over time, according to an Axios report that quoted Nicholas Lin, a product leader at Anthropic. “I’d watch that closely,” said Durr. “A meeting participant that acts on its own is a different product, and it starts a different governance conversation.” Claude Meetings is available in beta for customers with Claude Team and Enterprise payment plans. The feature is on by default for Claude Team customers. Other Claude features announced Tuesday include Claude Whiteboard, a shared canvas for coworkers to use while brainstorming. Teams can discuss ideas and Claude turns this into a board with a timeline, task owners, and due dates. Anthropic Currently in beta for paid Claude plans, Claude Whiteboard is available in web, mobile, and desktop. Customers on Claude Team and Enterprise plans can also access whiteboards inside Claude Meetings. Claude Sheets, a collaborative spreadsheet tool, is also available in beta, while Claude Data, a tool for creating interactive visual charts and reports that was previously called Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. Both are included in paid Claude subscriptions. Anthropic Finally, Anthropic announced updates to its “interactive connectors” that embed third-party applications…
